requirements.text: Put incident number INC0000002 on hold as we are waiting for the user's response
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_002' AND status = 'on_hold' AND on_hold_reason = 'Awaiting Caller'
assumptions: two incidents carry number INC0000002 (INC_002 in ORG_001, INC_009 in ORG_002); the acting user USER_001 is in ORG_001, so INC_002, as the benchmark's SLA check also assumes
on_hold_reason not stated; 'waiting for the user's response' is the policy enumeration value Awaiting Caller (sections 6 and 9)
status in_progress -> on_hold is a valid transition (policy 3.3)

requirements.text: Put incident number INC0000002 on hold (the SLA timer must be paused)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_sla WHERE incident_sla_id = 'TSLA_002' AND incident_id = 'INC_002' AND stage = 'paused'
requirements.source: Verify if the SLA is paused if the incident is on hold.
assumptions: pause not stated in the request; policy section 6 requires stage = paused when the incident is on hold with on_hold_reason Awaiting Caller
TSLA_002 is the only SLA row for INC_002 on the seed

requirements.text: Send a reminder notification to the user to provide the unique serial number of his system
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 'NOTIF_008' AND incident_id = 'INC_002' AND email = 'benjamin.chen@techcorp.com' AND type = 'reminder' AND message LIKE '%serial%'
requirements.source: Verify if the reminder notification is sent.
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (NOTIF_008 after NOTIF_007); the only notification the task creates
'the user' is the incident's caller USER_005 Benjamin Chen, benjamin.chen@techcorp.com
incident_id = INC_002 added to the benchmark check: the reminder is about this incident
message LIKE '%serial%' added to the benchmark check: the request fixes the content (provide the serial number)
notification subject and status not fixed by request or policy; not tested

requirements.text: Put incident number INC0000002 on hold (boundary: the other incident with that number)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_009' AND status = 'in_progress' AND on_hold_reason IS NULL
assumptions: INC_009 (ORG_002) also carries number INC0000002; a lookup by number alone could sweep it in, so it keeps its seed status and empty hold reason

requirements.text: Put incident number INC0000002 on hold (boundary: the other incident's SLA)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_sla WHERE incident_sla_id = 'TSLA_007' AND incident_id = 'INC_009' AND stage = 'completed'
assumptions: the SLA of the same-numbered incident in ORG_002 must not be paused

requirements.text: Send a reminder notification to the user (boundary: none for the other incident with that number)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE incident_id = 'INC_009'
assumptions: the ORG_002 incident INC_009 has no notifications on the seed and must gain none

notes:
disagreement: missing requirement: a stay that TSLA_007, the SLA of the ORG_002 incident INC_009 that shares number INC0000002, stays completed; one pass has it, the other does not; kept because the number names two incidents, so a lookup by number could pause the wrong SLA without touching INC_009 itself, and only this stay would catch that.
disagreement: missing requirement: a stay that no notification is created for INC_009; one pass has it, the other does not; kept because a reminder sent for both same-numbered incidents would pass the anchored NOTIF_008 requirement and the INC_009 status stay, and only this stay would catch the second message.
disagreement: value: the INC_009 stay's cells: one pass tests status = 'in_progress' and on_hold_reason IS NULL, the other status only; chose both cells, the tighter predicate, since both hold on the seed and putting INC_009 on hold sets the reason as well as the status.
The number INC0000002 is duplicated across organisations; the acting user's organisation resolves it to INC_002, which matches the benchmark's checks. The incident's own status change is not tested by the benchmark, so that requirement is new. The notification requirement keeps the benchmark's anchor and cells and adds incident_id and a message predicate from the request's words.
